page: Microsoft Azure E48bds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is built on dedicated x86_64 Intel processor architecture, supplying 48 dedicated virtual cores. It features 384.0 GB of total system RAM, corresponding to an allocation of 8.0 GB of memory per core. Compute and memory components are paired with 2,835 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, and the instance architecture is designed to support Azure Premium Storage for high-throughput block operations. The system contains no discrete GPUs and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From an engineering and architectural perspective, the 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio qualifies this configuration for memory-bound tasks requiring substantial headroom per thread. The direct inclusion of 2,835 GB of local NVMe SSD media delivers low-latency scratch disk capabilities, eliminating block storage overhead for temporary files, cache indices, and swap arrays. Because the vCPUs are dedicated, virtualization overhead is minimized, avoiding noisy-neighbor CPU throttling. Cost efficiency derives from high resource density, combining compute, high-capacity RAM, and high-speed local disk into a single node rather than distributing those requirements across clustered, fragmented smaller instances.

This virtual machine profile is suited for memory-intensive enterprise workloads that depend simultaneously on high capacity RAM and swift disk transactions. Core use cases include large relational databases, in-memory datastores such as Redis or Memcached clusters, data warehousing staging nodes, distributed ETL batch processing, and enterprise resource planning backend engines.
description: Microsoft Azure E48bds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine deployed via Microsoft Hyper-V, tailored for high-demand enterprise software and database infrastructure. Storage capabilities include a bundled 2,835 GB local NVMe SSD alongside Premium Storage support designed for high block storage throughput. The hardware configuration features zero onboard graphics processing units and allocates no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, aligning networking setups toward private enterprise boundaries. Operating without shared CPU contention, this profile balances substantial core counts with high random read and write local storage capacity. It is architecturally suited for relational databases, enterprise transactional workloads, in-memory caching solutions, and large-scale data analytics pipelines requiring high RAM capacity coupled with low-latency scratch storage.
